analysis.body:
# Grid Interconnection and Data Center Energy Demand

Across the five major US grid operators tracked here, 8,378 generation and storage projects totaling 1.33 million MW are in interconnection queues as of mid-September 2026. ERCOT dominates this total with 438,086 MW across 1,778 requests, followed by NYISO at 319,115 MW and MISO at 299,721 MW. While these queue totals represent planned supply, not data center demand itself, the composition matters: battery storage alone accounts for 327,000 MW across the queues, and natural gas additions total 184,344 MW. This pattern—storage and gas growth running parallel—tracks the profile of load that data centers impose: steady baseline consumption with acute peaks.

Commercial electricity sales across eight major states totaled 54,797 MWh in the most recent period, at an average price of $14.42 per MWh, though prices ranged sharply from $8.66 in Texas to $27.33 in California. Data centers are billed mostly within the commercial sector, making these sales volumes a proxy for their load rather than a direct measure. Texas leads absolute consumption at 15,754 MWh, followed by California at 10,025 MWh and Virginia at 7,771 MWh—the same three states that host the most interconnection activity and where large cloud and AI infrastructure clusters operate.

Solar capacity dominates new generation across queues, with 331,861 MW requested, but the queues also show 117,946 MW of new wind and 327,000 MW of storage: a portfolio built to serve variable and intensive simultaneous load. Watch whether MISO and SPP queue processing accelerates to match ERCOT's absorption pace, as delays in Midwestern and southern interconnections could constrain AI data center expansion in those regions.
